subject: Deployment topology constraints and next-action map for CloudWorks
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Terry Huang <terry@cloudworks.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 Oct 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment topology constraints and next-action map for CloudWorks

Hi Terry —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and a proposed set of next actions so we keep momentum while your infra team aligns internally. I summarized the call into pain / goals / constraints and flagged the technical items we said we'd follow up on.

Pain points (as you described)
- Unpredictable p95 latency at peak (spikes to ~220ms currently for 512-token completions).
- High token cost on current managed endpoints; need predictable unit economics.
- Lockbox requirement: traffic must stay inside our VPC for PHI-handling endpoints; SOC 2 evidence required.

Primary goals
- P95 <= 120ms for 512-token generative responses in us-west region.
- Baseline throughput target: 80 sustained requests/s with bursts to 200 for short periods.
- Deterministic failover plan if dedicated pool hits capacity.

Key constraints you flagged
- Must run inside customer-managed VPC for sensitive endpoints (private control plane).
- Single-region primary with cross-region read-only fallback (no active-active for now).
- Procurement/contracting window: aiming for signed pilot in 6 weeks.

What Redwood will deliver (agreed follow-ups)
- Preliminary sizing and three topology options (private dedicated pool, hybrid private-hosted split, hosted with strict routing) — deliverable by Monday 10/31 EOD. Attachment: topology-sketch.png (sketch + short notes).
- Ballpark cost estimate and canary plan for a 4-week pilot (attachment: mvp-canary-plan.md).
- SOC 2 artifacts checklist and recommended audit window; will get security partner to join next call if needed.

Immediate asks from you
- Confirm the p95 target above and whether 512-token is the correct baseline.
- Confirm which APIs will need VPC-only routing vs. which can be routed through hosted endpoints during pilot.
- If possible, please share a simple QPS/day histogram or peak windows for the last 30 days.

Next steps / owners
- Monica (me): send sizing + topology options (due 10/31 EOD) — attachment: sizing-estimate.csv
- Markus (cc): technical runbook draft + fallback patterns (due 10/31 11:59pm PT)
- Terry / CloudWorks: confirm p95 baseline and VPC vs hosted splits by end of day Monday 11/1.

If that matches what you remember, I’ll queue the sizing work and pull Ben in for pricing guidance. Thanks again — good call.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Monica — thanks for the thorough summary. A few clarifications inline and answers to your asks.

> Pain points
> - Unpredictable p95 latency at peak (spikes to ~220ms currently for 512-token completions).

Yes that's accurate — 512-token baseline is right. The 220ms spikes were happening during our 5–6pm PST batch jobs plus user traffic.

> Primary goals
> - P95 <= 120ms for 512-token generative responses in us-west region.

We agree to target p95 120ms for the pilot; if you can show a canary that demonstrates ~130ms we can accept that as a step-down target during initial ramp.

> Key constraints you flagged
> - Must run inside customer-managed VPC for sensitive endpoints (private control plane).

Correct — all PHI-tagged requests must never traverse external networks. Non-PHI traffic can use hosted endpoints.

Quick answers to your asks:
- Confirm p95 baseline: 512-token — confirmed.
- VPC-only vs hosted split: PHI endpoints = VPC-only; everything else can route hosted during pilot.
- QPS/day histogram: attached a one-page peak-hour CSV. We'll upload a clean histogram to the shared Drive later today.

One additional ask: can you include an explicit fallback model suggestion (smaller quantized variant) that covers 90–150 RPS peaks but with slightly degraded quality — we need that to justify the autoscaling guardrails in our SRE playbook.

Thanks — can we tentatively schedule the tech sync with Markus for Tues 11/2 10:00am PT?

-Terry

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Deployment topology constraints and next-action map for CloudWorks

Terry — quick technical notes and a recommended topology based on the targets (p95 120ms @ 80rps baseline, bursts to 200).

Short answer / recommendation:
- Pilot: Dedicated private pool (single-region us-west-2) with 4x A100-equivalent inference nodes running quantized 8-bit model variant (we recommend redwood/xl-q8y). Enable KV cache for prompt prefixes and continuous batching window tuned to 15–20ms.
- Canary fallback: Route excess traffic to two smaller q4 models in hosted mode (redwood/xl-q4s) with automatic percentage-based spillover; implement weighted routing to preserve latency SLOs.

Why this topology:
- Dedicated private pool gives predictability and avoids cross-network KMS constraints for PHI.
- Quantized 8-bit keeps token cost reasonable while preserving quality for your use case; fallback q4 buys throughput at lower compute cost.
- KV cache reduces repeated prefix tokenization and cuts effective token cost for multi-turn flows.

Sizing notes (see sizing-estimate.csv):
- Estimated baseline cluster: 4 nodes @ 80rps sustained (512-token average) -> p95 projection ~95–115ms with 8-bit quant and KV cache enabled.
- Burst headroom via autoscaling: add 2 nodes ramped on sustained 90s windows; short bursts handled by routing to hosted q4 fallback.

Security & network:
- Use Redwood Private deployment with customer-managed VPC peering and strict subnet egress rules. We can set up an initial one-way egress allowlist for telemetry and trace collection only.
- SOC 2 artifacts: we will share the standard evidence bundle; if you want a dedicated attestation window, we can queue that with our compliance team.

Open items for your SRE team to confirm:
- KMS/HSM provider and whether we need HSM-backed signing inside the VPC.
- Acceptable downgrade quality level for q4 fallback (we should define a fidelity guardrail).

I'll attach the sizing-estimate.csv. Happy to walk through the math on Tues 11/2 at 10am PT.

-Markus
